name: Bundy and Coke
description: Bundaberg rum and Coke, poured heavy. Queensland's contribution to world drinking, and defended with real feeling.
funFact: Bundaberg Rum has been distilled in Queensland since 1888 from local sugarcane molasses, and its polar bear mascot was introduced in the 1960s to suggest it could ward off the cold.

steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Pour in the rum.
Top with cold cola.
Stir once and squeeze in a lime wedge if you like.

name: Fluffy Duck
description: Advocaat, gin and lemonade with a float of cream. Pale, foamy and unapologetically 1970s — Australia never let it go.
funFact: Australian RSL clubs and country pubs kept the Fluffy Duck on the menu long after the rest of the world moved on, which is why it now reads as Australian rather than as generic seventies.

steps: Shake the advocaat, gin and orange juice with ice.
Strain into an ice-filled highball glass.
Top with lemonade and stir once.
Float the cream over the back of a spoon.
Garnish with a cherry and an orange slice.

name: Lemon Lime and Bitters
description: Lemonade, lime cordial and Angostura over ice. Effectively alcohol-free, and the most Australian thing you can order at a bar without ordering beer.
funFact: Australians call it an LLB and drink it by the jug at surf clubs and country pubs; the bitters are the only alcohol, at a level low enough that it is routinely served to children.

steps: Dash the Angostura into the bottom of a tall glass and swirl to coat.
Add the lime cordial.
Fill with ice.
Top with cold lemonade and stir once to bring the pink through.
Garnish with a lemon wedge.

name: Kava
description: Pounded kava root steeped in water and drunk from a coconut shell in one go. No alcohol at all, and it still changes the evening.
glassware: Coconut shell bilo, from a tanoa bowl
funFact: The kavalactones numb the mouth and relax the body without any alcohol involved. Fijian protocol is exact: clap once before you take the bilo, drink it in one, clap three times after, and say 'maca'.

ingredients.item: A cloth strainer and a tanoa bowl

steps: Put the powdered kava root into a cloth bag or muslin square.
Submerge it in cool water in a wide tanoa bowl.
Knead and squeeze the bag underwater for several minutes until the water turns muddy brown.
Wring out the cloth and discard the spent root.
Serve in coconut-shell bilos, filled and drunk in one — clap once before, three times after.

name: L&P and Vodka
description: Lemon & Paeroa — New Zealand's own lemony mineral soda — lengthening a shot of vodka. 'World famous in New Zealand', as the bottle says.
funFact: L&P was originally made by mixing lemon juice with mineral water from a spring at Paeroa; the town has a giant L&P bottle on the main road, which is the country's most photographed soft-drink monument.

steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Pour in the vodka and the lemon juice.
Top with cold L&P.
Stir once and garnish with a lemon wedge.
